facts.text: Calming rooms are listed at Vine Street Village and Mai Thai's Market. Sensory bags are available to check out at the Welcome Center.
quote: Calming Room Locations: Vine Street Village and Mai Thai’s Market
Sensory bags filled with oral motor chewy tubes, fidgets, noise-canceling headphones, sunglasses, etc. (Available for check-out at the Welcome Center)

facts.text: The Zoo publishes social and video narratives for general visits and several individual experiences.
quote: Social Narratives Going to the Zoo Social Narrative Going to the Zoo Video Narrative Roo Valley Social Narrative Roo Valley Video Social Narrative Giraffe Feeding Social Narrative Giraffe Feeding Video Social Narrative Blakely’s Barnyard Bonanza Social Narrative Cheetah Encounter Social Narrative

facts.text: Selected family restrooms include adult changing tables. A courtesy cart can assist visitors with mobility concerns along a fixed return route to Vine Street Village.
quote: Vine Street Village 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs; transfer board available in Welcome Center)

The Zoo offers a Courtesy Cart service for those with mobility concerns who need assistance returning to the front of the Zoo and is on a first-come first-served basis. This cart has a predetermined path starting from the Grove food truck area back to Vine Street Village.

facts.text: An Access Pass lets visitors who have significant difficulty standing or waiting queue outside the physical line for selected rides and experiences, with the same wait time.
quote: The Access Pass is available for visitors who may have significant trouble standing/waiting in line at the train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience, or Roo Valley. Using the Access Pass, visitors will wait the same length of time as the line, but outside of the traditional physical line.

facts.text: The Zoo is built on a hill and has many inclines. It reports many benches and rest areas, and staff can point out less steep paths.
quote: The Cincinnati Zoo is one of the oldest zoos in the nation, and was built on a hill. Please be advised that the Zoo has many inclines. We are happy to have many benches and rest areas throughout the Zoo, and any of our employees can guide you to paths that will be less steep.

facts.text: The Safari Train plays artificial chugging and whistle sounds and rings a bell at every crossing; the Zoo warns that guests sensitive to loud noises may be uncomfortable.
quote: Note: the train produces artificial chugging noises, an artificial train whistle sound, and will sound a bell at every train crossing. In addition, the train may produce loud grinding noises against the tracks. Guests with sensitivity to loud noises may become uncomfortable during the train ride.

facts.text: Manual wheelchairs, ECVs and strollers are rented at the Welcome Center in Historic Vine Street Village; a limited number can be reserved online at least 24 hours ahead.
quote: The Zoo has single and double strollers, manual wheelchairs, and electric wheelchairs that are available for rent at the Welcome Center, located in Historic Vine Street Village. We have a limited inventory and provide these items on a first-come, first-serve basis. There are a limited number of each item that can be reserved online ahead of time. Online reservations must be made at least 24 hours in advance.

facts.text: Visitors with an accessible placard are always allowed to park in Vine Lot, even when it is full for other traffic.
quote: Visitors with handicap/accessible placards will always be allowed to park in Vine Lot, even if the lot is full for other incoming traffic.

facts.text: Outside food, drinks and coolers are welcome (no glass or alcohol). The Visitor Experience team may store medical equipment or a medical cooler case by case.
quote: Visitors are welcome to bring their own food, beverages, and coolers into the Zoo! Glass and outside alcohol are prohibited.
The Visitor Experience team may be able to store medical equipment or a cooler for medical needs on a case-by-case basis.

facts.text: When a visitor requires a caregiver’s assistance, one caregiver can receive a free ticket by identifying themselves at the ticketing windows. The visitor and any additional caregivers need paid admission.
quote: If a caregiver is required to assist a visitor during their Zoo visit, one caregiver can receive a FREE admission ticket. The caregiver needs to identify that they are a caregiver at the ticketing windows to receive free admission. The visitor requiring a caregiver, and any additional caregivers, will need to purchase an admission ticket to enter the Zoo.

facts.text: Sensory-friendly restrooms have manual-flush toilets and paper towels instead of hand dryers.
quote: Sensory-Friendly restrooms include manual flush toilets instead of automatic flush, and paper towels instead of hand dryers.

facts.text: Therapy and emotional support animals are not permitted.
quote: Therapy or emotional support animals are not permitted in the Zoo.

facts.text: The zoo lists 20 designated accessible parking spaces in Vine Lot (Lot A) at 3427 Vine Street. Display your accessible placard to the parking attendants.
quote: Vine Lot (Lot A) located at 3427 Vine Street – 20 dedicated handicap/accessible parking spots
Please have your placard visible to attendants when entering Vine Lot.

facts.text: The zoo lists adult changing tables in two sensory-friendly family restrooms at Vine Street Village and two at the Picnic Shelters. It gives a height of 31 inches and a 400-pound capacity for these tables; a transfer board is available at the Welcome Center. These are published specifications, not Threshold measurements.
quote: Vine Street Village 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs; transfer board available in Welcome Center)
Picnic Shelters 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs)

facts.text: Each calming room accommodates one family at a time, first come, first served. The rooms stay locked until an employee opens them. Ask an employee, visit the Welcome Center or call 513-475-6198; if a room is occupied, staff can suggest alternative calm spaces.
quote: Each Calming Room can accommodate one family at a time, on a first-come, first-serve basis. To utilize the Calming Room at any point during your Zoo visit, please contact any employee, visit the Welcome Center, or call our Visitor Experience team at 513-475-6198. They will give you directions to meet an employee in the entry area. The door to the Calming Rooms is locked and can only be accessed by an employee. If the Calming Room is in use when you request it, the Visitor Experience team will advise alternative locations for a calm space.

facts.text: The courtesy cart returns from the Grove food-truck area to Vine Street Village. Request it through Public Safety at 513-475-6112 or the Guest Services podium across from Mai Thai’s Marketplace. It is not a continuously running shuttle and may involve a wait.
quote: This cart has a predetermined path starting from the Grove food truck area back to Vine Street Village. To request the Courtesy Cart, please contact Public Safety at (513)475-6112, or visit the Guest Services Podium across from Mai Thai’s Marketplace. This service is not a constantly running shuttle, and you may experience a brief wait time.

facts.text: The courtesy cart takes one mobility device at a time; some devices may not fit under the manufacturer’s safety rules. It cannot be reserved for groups, and service is first come, first served.
quote: The Courtesy Cart can accommodate 1 mobility device at a time. Please note that due to manufacturer safety regulations, some mobility devices may not fit on the cart. The Courtesy Cart is not available for group reservation.
The Zoo offers a Courtesy Cart service for those with mobility concerns who need assistance returning to the front of the Zoo and is on a first-come first-served basis.

facts.text: If you need a rental wheelchair to enter the zoo, ask a parking attendant for help retrieving one. The zoo warns that wheelchair availability varies and is not guaranteed.
quote: If you plan to rent a manual or electric wheelchair and need it to enter the Zoo, please alert a parking attendant and they will assist you with retrieving one (availability of wheelchairs may vary and is not guaranteed).

facts.text: The zoo gives the ordinary Safari Train boarding step as 19 inches and the doorway as 14 inches wide by 51 inches high. Its separate wheelchair car holds one wheelchair, with a ramp boarding doorway listed as 32 inches wide by 50 inches high; ask an employee for boarding and wheel-lock assistance.
quote: Boarding the train requires visitors to step up 19” and to clear a 14”w x 51”h entry into the car.

The Safari Train has an accessible train car that can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. The accessible car is 56″ long and 37″ wide. Boarding the train using our accessible ramp requires visitors to clear a 32”w x 50”h entry into the car. To use the accessible train car, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.

facts.text: The carousel can take one wheelchair at a time with staff ramp-boarding and wheel-lock assistance. For both train and carousel, some personal mobility devices may require transfer to a zoo-provided manual wheelchair because of the rides’ specifications.
quote: The Conservation Carousel can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. To ride the carousel in a wheelchair, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.

Note: due to the manufacturer and safety specifications of our train and carousel, some personal mobility devices may not be allowed on the accessible section of our rides and may require guests to transfer to a Zoo provided manual wheelchair.

facts.text: The zoo cannot refrigerate food or medicine; visitors may bring a cooler for items that need to stay chilled. Case-by-case storage of medical items is a separate service: ask at the Welcome Center or email at least two days ahead to coordinate.
quote: The Zoo is unable to provide refrigeration of any kind for any items that may need to be kept cool. We advise that if you require certain items (food or medicine) to be kept chilled, you may bring in a cooler with you.

The Visitor Experience team may be able to store medical equipment or a cooler for medical needs on a case-by-case basis. For more information about storing medical items or places to comfortably administer these items, please visit the Welcome Center upon arrival, or email [email protected] at least (2) days prior to your visit to coordinate.

facts.text: Cups of water are free at open dining locations. The zoo says its drinking fountains are turned off for the winter season; an open fountain should not be assumed during a winter visit.
quote: Cups of water are available at no cost at any open dining location. Water fountains are available throughout the Zoo (these are turned off during the Winter season).

facts.text: Ask for an Access Pass at the Welcome Center, train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience or Roo Valley. Staff give a lanyard with a return time based on the queue; return at or after that time and hand it to staff for the separate entrance.
quote: To use an Access Pass, ask an employee at the Welcome Center, train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience, or Roo Valley for a pass: they will calculate the wait time and give you a lanyard with the time you are allowed to ride/enter the experience. At or after your time has passed, bring the lanyard to an employee at the ride or experience, and they will take it and allow you onto the next ride or experience through a separate entrance.

facts.text: Visitors needing wheelchair seating or other seating accommodations are asked to notify the box office in advance and allow extra time on arrival for staff to arrange seating.
quote: Please notify the box office in advance if you require wheelchair seating or have special seating needs and our staff will be happy to accommodate you. Please allow extra time at the box office to enable our staff to comfortably facilitate your seating needs.

facts.text: The box office publishes 513-479-6783 as its contact number. Contact it before attending if seating or route arrangements need confirmation.
quote: Box Office Phone Number: 513-479-6783

facts.text: Seating opens 30 minutes before each performance.
quote: Seating opens 30 minutes prior to each performance.

facts.text: If you leave during a performance, readmittance is at the house manager's discretion; latecomers are also seated at the house manager's discretion.
quote: Latecomers will be seated at the discretion of the House Manager.
Should you leave the theatre during a performance, readmittance will be at the discretion of the House Manager.

facts.text: Street parking is available on most main and side streets; check the parking meters for their hours.
quote: Street Parking – Available on most main and side streets. Please pay attention to parking meters for effective times.

facts.text: Once a show opens, its webpage links the complete program for reading before or after attending. A lobby QR code also links the full program; abbreviated printed programs are available at performances.
quote: Programs: Abbreviated physical programs are available for performances. Patrons can also scan a QR Code, displayed in the Lobby, to view the complete program online (a link to the program is also available on each show’s website page, once’s the show opens, so patrons can read the program before or after the production).

facts.text: The ticket-policy page asks reserved-ticket holders to claim tickets at least 10 minutes before showtime and prepaid online-ticket holders by showtime; unclaimed tickets may be released. Latecomers may be denied admission depending on the production. Weather or illness cancellations are posted on the website and box-office line.
quote: All reserved tickets must be claimed at least 10 minutes prior to show time and pre-paid tickets (online sales) must be claimed by show time. Falcon reserves the right to release any unclaimed tickets.
Latecomers may be denied admission depending upon the demands or structure or a particular production.

If a performance needs to be cancelled due to inclement weather, illness or other unforeseen events we will notify public information sources. We will also post cancellation information on our Website and our Box Office phone line. Please call our box office for ticket exchanges/refunds.

facts.text: The box office and Will Call open one hour before performances. Online sales close one hour before curtain; the box-office phone takes voicemail at 513-479-6783.
quote: Box Office/Will Call opens 1 hour prior to each performance.
Box Office telephone line is available at all times via voice mail (513) 479-6783.
Online ticket sales close 1 hour prior to curtain for all performances.

facts.text: Falcon lists public parking at 707 Monmouth Street beside The Pepper Pod, 7th and Orchard behind La Mexicana Grocery, and 117 E. 5th Street behind Truist Bank. Its directions page does not establish step-free connections or designated accessible spaces in those lots.
quote: Public Parking Lots 117 E. 5th Street, behind Truist Bank 707 Monmouth Street, next to The Pepper Pod 7th Street and Orchard, behind La Mexicana Grocery

facts.text: Falcon’s health page asks patrons who feel ill to contact the box office about transferring or refunding tickets if necessary. It welcomes masks and says a hand-sanitizer station is available in the lobby.
quote: If you are feeling sick or demonstrating ANY signs of illness, please stay home. Contact the Falcon Theatre Box Office with regards to tickets you may have purchased and we will either transfer or refund your tickets if necessary. MASKS WELCOME : All Patrons entering Falcon Theatre are welcome to wear masks if it makes you feel more comfortable to do so. A hand sanitizer station will always be available in the lobby.

facts.text: The Attraction Accessibility Program gives guests with mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments access to attractions. It does not provide immediate boarding.
quote: To provide equal access for all Guests, we have developed a program that allows Guests with mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments to access attractions.
Kings Island's Attraction Accessibility Program is designed to provide equal access to all Guests and does not provide immediate boarding onto attractions.

facts.text: Guests seeking accommodations for mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments are encouraged to register for an IBCCES Accessibility Card online or through its app. The park describes an application and documentation upload before the digital card is available.
quote: Guests with mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments who request reasonable accommodations are encouraged to obtain the IBCCES Accessibility Card (IAC) by registering at

or via the Accessibility Card mobile App. Once a Guest has filled out the online application and uploaded necessary documentation into a secure online portal, they will be able to access their digital Accessibility Card.

facts.text: Manual wheelchairs and electric wheelchairs with a sun-shade canopy can be rented for the day; the rentals page lists the current prices.
quote: Manual Wheelchair Rental Only $25 *Plus processing fees of up to $9.99 & applicable taxes. Rent a manual wheelchair for your visit to the park. Valid on the date selected at purchase.

Electric Wheelchair + Canopy Rental Only $65 *Plus processing fees of up to $9.99 & applicable taxes. Rent an electric wheelchair with a sun shade canopy for your visit to the park. Valid on the date selected at purchase.

facts.text: Guests with full arm (elbow-restricting) or full leg (knee-restricting) casts or braces are restricted from most rides and water slides at Kings Island and Soak City.
quote: Guests with full arm (elbow restricted) and full leg (knee restricted) casts, or braces, are restricted from MOST rides and water slides at Kings Island and Soak City.

facts.text: With at least one week's notice, the park provides ASL interpretation for live shows at its entertainment venues. Braille and large-print copies of the Guest Accessibility Guide are at Guest Services in limited numbers.
quote: If requested at least 1 week in advance, Kings Island will provide American Sign Language (ASL) Interpretation for live shows featured at our live entertainment venues.
Braille and large print copies of the Guest Accessibility Guide are available at Guest Services. There are a limited number of guides available on a first-come, first-served basis.

facts.text: White canes can be used on many attractions, but may need to be collapsed and secured, stored or left with a non-rider where they could be a hazard.
quote: White Canes can be used to access many of our attractions. White Canes may need to be collapsed and safely secured, stored, or left with a non-rider on attractions where they could be a hazard.

facts.text: Service animals are welcome; a relief area is next to the restroom at Queen City Stunt Coaster. Service animals are not permitted in water attractions, wet decks, wading pools or lazy rivers.
quote: Service animals are welcome at Kings Island.
A relief area is located adjacent to the restroom at Queen City Stunt Coaster.
Service animals are not permitted in water attractions, wet decks, wading pools, or lazy rivers.

facts.text: Present your IBCCES Accessibility Card at Guest Services on arrival to explain your accommodation needs; only IBCCES issues the card, not Kings Island. Each ride's Safety Guide sign shows where program guests enter.
quote: Guests will present the IBCCES Accessibility Card to Guest Services upon their arrival at the park to express their accommodation needs.
Only IBCCES can issue the IBCCES Accessibility Card, and not Kings Island.
Information about where Guests access the ride is posted on each attraction's Safety Guide sign.

facts.text: The park prohibits leg prostheses on Banshee, Delirium, Diamondback, Invertigo and Orion. It says guests with certain amputations may be eligible for a separate supplemental harness on Orion, Diamondback and Banshee if remaining arm and leg remnants can be secured; Guest Services determines eligibility.
quote: Guests with leg prostheses are not permitted to ride Banshee, Delirium, Diamondback, Invertigo, or Orion.

Guests with certain amputations may be able to ride Orion, Diamondback, and Banshee with the use of a separate supplemental restraint harness, provided the Guest has remaining leg and arm remnants to be secured by the harness. Guests should check with Guest Services to determine if they are eligible to ride using the supplemental restraint harness.

facts.text: On most rides a service animal must stay with a non-riding member of your party; staff cannot take control of it.
quote: Due to the nature of most rides, service animals must remain with a non-riding member of your party. We are not permitted to take control of your service animal.

facts.text: Guests with medically required diets may bring small soft-sided coolers. Otherwise only unopened and empty water bottles and baby food are allowed.
quote: Unopened and empty water bottles and baby food are permitted. No other outside food, beverage, or snack items are permitted in Kings Island.
Individuals who have special dietary needs due to a medical condition may bring small soft sided coolers to accommodate such needs.

facts.text: For same-day re-entry, request a re-entry ticket at the Front Gate or Soak City exit; passholders may use their season-pass card. The FAQ says there is no re-entry after 6 p.m. on Halloween Haunt nights for either ticket holders or passholders. Keep the parking receipt if leaving and returning to the lot.
quote: If you wish to leave the park and return on the same day, please request a re-entry ticket at the Front Gate or Soak City exit. If you wish to leave the parking lot and re-enter, present your parking receipt to the attendant when you return. Passholders can re-enter by using their season pass card. Please be advised there is no re-entry after 6:00 PM during Halloween Haunt nights for both ticket holders and Passholders.

facts.text: Preferred Parking is next to the Front Gate; there are no Preferred spaces near the Soak City entrance.
quote: Get easy access to your car by parking right next to the Front Gate! Valid on the date selected only. Please be advised that there are no Preferred Parking spaces near the Soak City entrance.

facts.text: The attraction-access program does not waive ride requirements: the park says every guest must meet each attraction’s height and health restrictions. Guest Services asks questions about the physical criteria needed for the requested rides.
quote: All Guests are required to meet all riding requirements for every attraction, including height and health restrictions, to safely ride/participate.
Some questions are asked to ensure that the Guest has the required physical criteria in order to safely experience attractions.

facts.text: After requesting ASL interpretation in advance, check in at Guest Services on arrival to review the show schedule and choose performances.
quote: Upon arrival at the park, please check in with Guest Services to review our show schedule and determine your preferred showtimes and selections.

facts.text: During WinterFest, temperatures near freezing may stop some rides from operating under manufacturer guidelines. Cold weather can also affect live entertainment; admission does not establish that a particular experience will run.
quote: Please be advised that as temperatures approach freezing some rides may not be able to operate due to manufacturer guidelines. Colder temperatures also could impact live entertainment during WinterFest.

facts.text: The linked Guest Accessibility Guide lists car and van spaces in the main lots, first come, first served, with a valid disability placard or plate displayed. Ask at the parking toll booths for directions. If those spaces are full, it identifies a passenger drop-off near the main entrance.
quote: Accessible parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis within the main parking lots of the park. When you arrive at the parking toll booths, ask an Associate for instructions regarding where to proceed to the accessible parking lot. Both auto and van accessible spaces are provided. A valid disabled persons parking placard or license plate must be displayed at all times while parked in the designated accessible parking area. If the designated accessible parking area is full at the time of your arrival, members of your party may be dropped off at the main pick-up/drop-off area, near the main entrance to the park.

facts.text: The guide lists adult changing tables at the Family Care Center, near the Coconut Cove restroom, and in family restrooms inside the Front Gate and at Queen City Stunt Coaster, Invertigo and Banshee. It does not supply table dimensions or weight limits.
quote: Adult changing tables are located at the Family Care Center, near the Coconut Cove restroom, and the following family restrooms: inside Front Gate, Queen City Stunt Coaster, Invertigo, and Banshee.

facts.text: The guide lists private restrooms for visitors who need another person’s assistance at every restroom location, including First Aid, and wheelchair-accessible stalls in all restrooms. These are the park’s descriptions, not measured layouts.
quote: Private restroom facilities for Guest needing the assistance of another Guest are available at all restroom locations throughout the park, including First Aid. Wheelchair accessible stalls are located at all restrooms.

facts.text: The First Aid building in Planet Snoopy beside Charlie Brown’s Wind Up is listed as staffed from park opening to closing, with medical-equipment storage and medication refrigeration. A second First Aid location near the Soak City train station operates during Soak City hours.
quote: Our First Aid Building located in PLANET SNOOPY™(adjacent to Charlie Brown’s Wind Up) is staffed from park open to park close. Medical equipment storage and refrigeration for Guests with medication is offered at First Aid. In addition, a First Aid Building is located in Soak City near the T rain Station. This location is open during Soak City operating hours.

facts.text: The Rental Center is on the left just inside the Front Gate. The guide lists limited wheelchairs, ECVs and strollers, advance online wheelchair/ECV reservations, and on-site rentals while supplies last.
quote: A limited supply of wheelchairs, electric convenience vehicles (ECV), and strollers are available for rent at the Rental Center on the left, just inside the front gate. Online reservations are available for wheelchair/ECV rentals in advance of your visit. Reservations can be made by going to sixflags.com/kingsisland and visit the rentals page under the Tickets tab. Rentals are also available at the park while supplies last.

facts.text: Rented wheelchairs, ECVs and strollers may not leave the park gates or go to the parking lot. The guide offers staff help at that point but does not define a parking-lot wheelchair service; confirm how to reach or leave the rental counter.
quote: Wheelchairs, ECV’s, and strollers may not be taken out of the park gates or to the parking lot. However, a park Associate will be happy to provide any assistance you may need at that time.

facts.text: Kings Island says staff are not trained or permitted to transfer guests from wheelchairs into ride vehicles. It asks visitors to bring someone who can physically help when needed; transfer devices do not imply staff lifting assistance.
quote: Kings Island personnel are not trained in transferring Guests from wheelchairs to ride units and are not permitted to do so. Y ou should plan your visit with someone who can physically help you when necessary.

facts.text: The guide identifies wheelchair lifts to upper ride platforms at Banshee, Mystic Timbers and Orion. Use the call button at the base to request service. It describes manual-wheelchair alternatives where posted lift capacity or ECV attachments prevent use; ask staff about the particular device and lift.
quote: A wheelchair lift is available at Banshee, Mystic Timbers, and Orion to transport a Guest in a wheelchair to our second-story ride platform. Please use the call button at base of lift to request service. Manual wheelchairs are available at all locations with a wheelchair lift if weight exceeds the max posted capacity. If an ECV has attachments to the vehicle which could impede with the operation of a lift or with safe lift ingress and egress, please transfer to manual wheelchair. Applicable attachments would include canopies, antennae, umbrellas, awnings, etc. Please ask an Associate at each location for assistance.

facts.text: For water-wheelchair or pool-lift access, the guide directs visitors to the Aquatics Supervisory team. It lists water-wheelchair entry assistance at Coconut Cove, Splash River’s entry area, Tidal Wave Bay and Breakers Bay; the chair can be shared by multiple guests during the day. The guide also sets water-depth and rider criteria; ask the team which apply to the intended attraction.
quote: A water wheelchair is available for Guests requiring additional assistance when gaining access into Coconut Cove, Splash River (Entry Area), Tidal Wave Bay, and Breakers Bay. The water wheelchair may be used by multiple Guests on the same day.
During your visit, please speak to a member of our Aquatics Supervisory team to obtain access to the water wheelchair or pool lift and for further accessibility information.

While in a/the wave pool, the water level may not exceed the height of the seat on the chair. Guests participating in a wave pool are permitted to use a personal wheelchair. Personal wheelchairs are permitted up to the seat's water depth. Guests utilizing wheelchairs will not be required to utilize a lifejacket while in the wave pool only if their height exceeds 52" tall and meet all other rider criteria for the attraction.

In order to participate on most attractions, Guests must have independent seated postural control, appropriate center of gravity, appropriated observed behavior, and the ability to enter and exit the attraction safely.

facts.text: The guide lists transfer devices available on request at Banshee, Beast, Racer, Mystic Timbers, The Bat and Woodstock Express. Ask the ride team how a device is used and whether it suits the intended transfer; the listing does not promise staff lifting.
quote: T ransfer devices, when requested, can be used to assist a Guest out of a wheelchair and into a ride unit. The following rides are equipped with a transfer device: Banshee, Beast, Racer, Mystic Timbers, The Bat, and Woodstock Express.

Kings Island personnel are not trained in transferring Guests from wheelchairs to ride units and are not permitted to do so. Y ou should plan your visit with someone who can physically help you when necessary.

facts.text: The guide identifies ride vehicles with removable sides at Queen City Stunt Coaster and SNOOPY’S Soap Box Racers to help with wheelchair-to-seat transfers. Tell an associate at the ride if you want to use that vehicle; riders still need to meet its eligibility criteria.
quote: Specific ride vehicles are equipped with removable sides at Queen City Stunt Coaster and SNOOPY’S™ Soap Box Racers. These vehicles may further assist Riders in transferring from their wheelchair to the ride unit. Please inform an Associate at the ride if you wish to use that vehicle.
All Guests are required to meet all riding requirements for every attraction, including height and health restrictions in order to safely ride/participate.

facts.text: On most rides, a service animal must stay with a non-riding member of the visitor’s party. Kings Island says staff are not permitted to take control of the animal; ask Guest Services about Rider Swap rather than assuming staff can provide animal care.
quote: Due to the nature of most rides, service animals must remain with a non-Riding member of your party. We are not permitted to take control of your service animal.
Guests may take advantage of our Rider Swap policy for staying with the service animal. Visit Guest Services for more information

facts.text: In Soak City, the guide places a service-animal relief area by the restrooms near Tropical Plunge. Owners must dispose of their animal’s waste; this does not remove the separate restrictions on animals entering water attractions or wet decks.
quote: A Service Animal Relief Area is located in the grassy area next to Queen City Stunt Coaster and in Soak City by the restrooms near T ropical Plunge. Owners are responsible for disposing of their animal’s waste. Please look for this designated sign:
Service animals are not permitted in water attractions, wet decks, wading pools, or lazy rivers.

facts.text: There are four designated accessible parking spaces with access aisles, a front-entrance curb cut, and automatic door buttons on the interior and exterior entrance doors.
quote: Four designated accessible parking spaces, each with access aisles Front-entrance curb cut Automatic interior and exterior door-open buttons at the entrance

facts.text: An oversized elevator serves all floors, and the theater has two designated wheelchair seats with companion seating.
quote: Oversized elevator access to all floors
Two designated mobility-device-accessible seats in the theater (with companion seating)

facts.text: Mobility-device-accessible restroom stalls are on the first and third floors.
quote: Mobility-device-accessible bathroom stalls on first and third floors

facts.text: Room signs are in Braille and gallery signage is high-contrast and large-print. With advance notice, tactile tours of selected artworks and building features are offered.
quote: Room signage in Braille
High-contrast, large-print gallery signage With advance notice, the Fitton Center also offers tactile tours, including selected artworks and building features

facts.text: With advance notice, support workers can accompany registered students in classes and workshops without paying a registration fee.
quote: With advance notice, the Fitton Center requires no class registration or enrollment fees for support workers to accompany/assist registered students during classes/workshops.

facts.text: Fitton lists height-adjustable tables in the basement studio and studio 104. It says room layouts in the Carruthers Signature Ballroom, Rotary Vista Room and Riverview Terrace can be arranged to accommodate mobility devices.
quote: Height-adjustable tables in basement studio and studio 104
Flexible room setup in the Carruthers Signature Ballroom and Rotary Vista Room– as well as on the Riverview Terrace – to accommodate all mobility devices

facts.text: Galleries close periodically for installations, so check the schedule. Accessibility questions: 513-863-8873 ext. 110 or frontdesk@fittoncenter.org.
quote: Galleries are periodically closed for the installation of new art, so please check the exhibition schedule before your visit.
please call 513-863-8873, ext. 110 or write frontdesk@fittoncenter.org

facts.text: Fitton’s event-rental FAQ lists a free 99-space parking lot for event guests and warns that it may be shared when multiple events take place. It also lists surrounding lots and street parking, without describing their access features.
quote: The Fitton Center has a parking lot with 99 spaces. It is free and available for use for you and your guests. Sometimes we have multiple events taking place and the parking lot is shared. There are other lots surrounding the Fitton Center as well as street parking.

facts.text: Fitton lists a mobility-device-accessible pottery wheel and ramp access to its movement studio. The page does not give wheel clearances, ramp dimensions or the route from the elevator.
quote: Mobility-device-accessible pottery wheel
Ramp-accessible movement studio

facts.text: Fitton’s camp procedures ask anyone needing accommodations for an education program to contact the Director of Education & Outreach before registering. This is an advance discussion, not confirmation that a particular accommodation is arranged.
quote: If a student believes that they will require accommodations to enable them to participate in our programs, please contact our Director of Education & Outreach before registration.

facts.text: People unable to leave home can call 859-291-6789 to request monthly pantry delivery. Be Concerned evaluates available volunteer resources before arranging this service; delivery is not guaranteed.
quote: Request Monthly Pantry Homebound Delivery If you are unable to leave your home and need assistance accessing food, please call us to request this assistance. This service is dependent upon volunteer support so we will need to evaluate the available resources.

facts.text: The Covington pantry asks households to register in person before arranging monthly shopping appointments. Registration requires photo ID for the head of household and a current-address document; other adults need a document showing the same address.
quote: Visit our location in Covington. Please visit us during our registration hours and provide the following information: Photo identification for the head of household A document with a current address (a piece of mail will work!) For any other adults in the household, a document with the same address as the head of household
Once you have registered, we will provide you with your first monthly pantry appointment. Monthly trips to the pantry do require an appointment.

facts.text: For each child in the household, the registration page asks for a birth certificate, Social Security card or report card. Confirm acceptable documents before travelling if you cannot supply these.
quote: A birth certificate, social security card or report card will be needed for each child in the household

facts.text: The contact page lists pantry registration Monday–Tuesday, 9 a.m.–noon. This differs from the separate Get Help page; call 859-291-6789 to confirm when to come.
quote: Pantry Registration Monday – Tuesday 9:00 AM – 12:00 PM

facts.text: The Get Help page instead lists Covington registration Monday–Friday, 1–3 p.m. This conflicts with the contact page’s morning schedule; do not assume either window is confirmed.
quote: Registration Hours Covington 1100 Pike Street 859-291-6789 Monday – Friday 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM

facts.text: The contact page lists pantry shopping by appointment on Tuesdays 4–5:30 p.m. and Wednesdays–Fridays 10 a.m.–noon. These are appointment windows, not walk-in registration hours.
quote: Pantry Hours by Appointment Tuesday 4:00 PM– 5:30 PM Wednesday – Friday 10:00 AM– 12:00 PM

facts.text: For an extreme or unexpected need, Be Concerned offers emergency food equivalent to a small grocery cart. People not already registered are asked questions to create an account; the Get Help page lists this assistance Monday–Friday, 1–3 p.m.
quote: If you are in an extreme or unexpected situation and need emergency food, we can provide you with the equivalent of a small grocery cart of food. If you are not registered with us, we will ask a few questions so that we can establish an account for you into our system. Our goal would be to work with you and bring you into our monthly pantry program.
Emergency Food Assistance Hours Covington 1100 Pike Street 859-291-6789 Monday – Friday 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM

facts.text: Monthly pantry shoppers choose their food rather than receiving a prepacked selection. The program lists staples, milk, eggs, frozen meat and fresh vegetables; dietary suitability and item availability still need confirmation.
quote: We offer a selection of canned goods, pasta, bread, cereal, crackers, milk, eggs, frozen meat and fresh vegetables in addition to seasonal items. Approximately 60-70 pounds of food is provided to each family. The most important element of our service is the opportunity for our customers to choose their pantry items. Nothing is pre-packaged for them.

facts.text: Be Concerned brings its monthly pantry program to several partner senior-living complexes in Northern Kentucky. The food-program page does not identify every eligible building; confirm whether yours participates.
quote: We partner with several senior living complexes in Northern Kentucky to bring our monthly pantry program to them. Our seniors have access to the variety of foods that are on site at our pantry.

facts.text: Betty’s Treasures at the Covington address is listed for shopping Monday–Friday, noon–3 p.m. The page does not describe the shop entrance, aisle widths or toilet facilities.
quote: Be Concerned Pantry & Betty’s Treasures Thrift Store Covington 1100 Pike Street Covington, KY 41011
Thrift Store Shopping Monday – Friday 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM

facts.text: The FAQ says thrift-store vouchers may be offered in certain circumstances after discussing the person’s situation and needed items. It does not promise a voucher for every visitor.
quote: We can offer vouchers to the thrift store in certain situations. We will work with you to understand your situation and needed items.

facts.text: Be Concerned says the former United Ministries building in Erlanger is no longer operating. It now describes monthly mobile pantries in Erlanger, Elsmere, Walton and Silver Grove; confirm the current site and date before travelling.
quote: In 2019, Be Concerned took over operation of the former United Ministries in Erlanger. The building is no longer in operation but paved the way for our current mobile pantries. We currently operate four monthly mobile pantries in Erlanger, Elsmere, Walton, and Silver Grove.
